headline: Former China Securities Regulator Sentenced to Death with Reprieve
summary: Wang Huimin, a former member of the Communist Party committee at the China Securities Regulatory Commission, was sentenced to death with a two-year reprieve over bribery charges involving over 436 million yuan.
why: The CSRC is China's primary securities and market regulator; high-profile corruption crackdowns reflect ongoing regulatory oversight of the financial sector.

impacts.name: Chinese Financial Services
impacts.why: Anti-corruption enforcement targeting former regulatory officials reinforces state oversight across domestic capital markets.
